newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling firm on steady dlr inflows.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling firm on steady dlr inflows.

text.p: Steady dollar inflows helped firm the Kenyan shilling against the dollar on Tuesday, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean of 55.26 shillings to the dollar, from 55.32 on Monday. Against sterling, the shilling was posted at 91.43 from 90.93.
Dealers said dollars streamed in from the agricultural sector, mainly tea, and from normal customer transactions.
Some said passive intervention from the central bank did not stop the firm tone of the shilling against the dollar. One dealer said the central bank bought dollars at 55.30.

"We are expecting some more dollar inflows from the tea and coffee sector today, but I don't see much movement in the shilling because these have already been picked up by the oil importers," another dealer said.

"The shilling looks comfortable around the 55.30 level. If all holds steady, and demand maintains its low tone, then we might not see much movement of the shilling below that level," another dealer added.
Thursday will be a public holiday.
The money market was a bit tight, with overnight rates quoted between 18 and 20 percent from 13 to 20 percent on Monday.
